title: sdet_plan
description: Backend SDET test plan produced by the sdet-plan-generator skill. Versioned output — scenarios are never deleted, only deprecated.

plan_version.description: Semantic version bumped on every generation or review run, e.g. '1.0', '1.1'

generation_mode.description: Mode of the last run that wrote this file

canonical_team_id.description: Stable team identifier resolved from team_registry.json. 'unknown' signals a registry miss — triggers a warning in qa_analysis.md and blocks downstream module path construction.

code_module.description: Exact test code module directory name from team_registry.json code.module. Consumed verbatim by automation-plan-generator for Java package path. null when team resolution failed.

scenario_id.description: Stable unique ID, e.g. SC-EPIC1122-001. Never reused.

source_ref.description: Pointer to originating AC / RFC step / PRD section, e.g. 'RFC-78:step-3 / AC-002'

generated_by_mode.description: Which pipeline mode CREATED this scenario. Set once at creation; never overwritten.

review_round.description: Which review round last modified this scenario. 0 = not yet reviewed. Incremented by Review mode runs.

provisional.description: True when approach_finalised:false or edge_case.inferred:true. Assertions may change.

status.description: Per-scenario human sign-off. The GENERATOR always writes 'draft' and must never write 'approved' — only a person sets that. 'in_review' = a reviewer picked it up. 'changes_requested' = feedback written into qa_analysis.md, Review-mode run pending. 'approved' = this scenario is cleared to flow downstream. 'deprecated' = human marked it for removal; the scenario is kept, not deleted, so downstream can detect the change. Distinct from the plan-root `status`: root says the plan has been through review at all, this says whether THIS scenario is signed off. A plan may be partially approved. Any run that changes this scenario's content resets it to 'draft'.

change_reason.description: One sentence — what changed and why. Set by retrigger and review modes.

is_delta.description: true for pass2 / retrigger / review-added scenarios

is_legacy_regression.description: true when scenario covers pre-existing regression coverage

is_dedup.description: true when this scenario duplicates ANOTHER SCENARIO IN THIS SAME PLAN. Written by dedup-generator (scenario mode), which reads only the plan and has no access to existing coverage. Do NOT use it for 'already covered by an existing regression test' — that is regression_action: 'reuse' plus existing_case_ref, written by sdet-plan-generator from regression_context.json. Both cause automation-plan-generator to skip the scenario, but they answer different questions and have different owners.

dedup_reason.description: Why this scenario was flagged is_dedup, naming the canonical scenario it duplicates (e.g. 'same arrange and outcome as SC-006'). Required whenever is_dedup is true — a bare flag is unauditable. Set by dedup-generator, never by sdet-plan-generator.

test_type.description: BrowserStack TestType — multi-select. Collect ALL applicable values (additive, not first-match). Serialised as comma-separated in CSV.

execution_mode.description: Manual when tags contain 'deferred' or 'underspecified'; Automatable otherwise

markets.description: Countries this scenario applies to. Maps to BrowserStack Country v2.

type_of_test.description: performance ONLY when tags contain load or nfr, i.e. the scenario measures a throughput or latency target. functional otherwise — including reliability, concurrency, security and compliance scenarios, which assert functional behaviour under adverse conditions rather than measuring performance.

human_corrected.description: false at generation time. Set to true when any Review run modifies or deprecates this scenario. Never reset. LLM accuracy signal.

human_correction_types.description: Accumulated correction types across all review rounds. field_change = field corrected by human; deprecated = LLM over-generated; missed_scenario = LLM failed to generate (set on review-added scenarios).

curl_reference.description: null for DB/infra-only steps with no HTTP call

tags.description: happy_path | negative | boundary | flag_on | flag_off | e2e | load | concurrency | security | reliability | compliance | nfr | deferred | underspecified | provisional

scenario_group.description: Key shared by scenarios resting on the same Arrange: identical precondition state and triggering call, differing only in the data row exercised. A test-design fact, not an automation instruction — it applies to Manual scenarios too, where it marks cases a human tester can run back-to-back off one setup. Standalone scenarios get a unique key. Format: {feature_component}-{behaviour}. Downstream consumers decide how to use it.

existing_testcase_ids.description: Existing BrowserStack case ids (e.g. TC-302383) this scenario extends, replaces, or re-runs under a new flag state. From regression_context.json only — never invented. Rendered into the Preconditions block and consumed downstream for @TestInfo.

owning_team.description: canonical_id of the team owning this scenario's SYSTEM UNDER TEST — the service whose contract the assertions are about, not the team whose feature triggered the work. Defaults to the primary canonical_team_id and is set explicitly on every scenario. automation-plan-generator resolves the code module and BrowserStack project from this, not from the root code_module.

browserstack_test_id.description: BrowserStack's own test-case id, assigned when this scenario is uploaded via the BrowserStack MCP. null until the upload runs — always emit the key so downstream readers never infer state from absence. Written back into the plan by the sync, never authored by the generator. DISTINCT from existing_testcase_ids[], which holds ids of cases that already existed BEFORE this plan (sourced from regression_context.json); this field is the id THIS scenario received.

existing_case_ref.description: The single BrowserStack case id this scenario duplicates or directly impacts, verbatim (e.g. 'TC-329330' or 'C3260998'). Set whenever is_legacy_regression is true because of a real match — is_legacy_regression true with no ref is a bare flag nobody can audit or trace back. Omit when the scenario is genuinely new. Use existing_testcase_ids[] when a scenario maps to several cases.

regression_action.description: What this scenario implies for existing automated coverage. 'none' = net-new; generate a new test method. 'reuse' = an existing case already covers this exact behaviour; emit the row so reviewers can see it exists, but generate no code. 'modify' = an existing test covers this surface and must be EDITED because the change alters what it should assert. 'modify' is the disposition most easily missed on backend: a response POJO that tolerates unknown fields lets the existing test keep PASSING after a field is added, while silently covering less — nobody re-runs their way to noticing that.

existing_test_ref.description: Repo location of the existing automated test this scenario reuses or modifies, copied from regression_context.regression_tests[].test_ref. REQUIRED when regression_action is 'modify' — an edit instruction cannot be emitted against a case id alone.

case_numbers.description: Numeric case ids this method implements, from @TestInfo(testCaseIds={...}).

change_required.description: What must change in the existing test and why. REQUIRED when regression_action is 'modify'. Name the assertion that becomes insufficient, not merely that the test is affected.

is_near_dedup.description: true when this scenario is a NEAR duplicate — overlapping but not identical, so it is surfaced for a human rather than flagged outright. Never auto-flag a near duplicate as is_dedup; automation-plan-generator does NOT skip on this field, so a near duplicate still becomes a test method unless a reviewer converts it.

llm_quality.description: LLM generation accuracy — populated at plan creation; updated after each Review run.

auto_approved.description: Scenarios not touched by any review round — LLM got them right

human_modified.description: Scenarios LLM generated but with incorrect fields (human corrected via Review)

human_deprecated.description: Scenarios LLM generated unnecessarily — duplicate or wrong (deprecated by human)

human_added.description: Scenarios LLM missed entirely — added from scratch by human via Review

llm_accuracy_pct.description: auto_approved / (auto_approved + human_modified + human_deprecated) × 100. null until first review round completes.

dedup_report.description: Written by dedup-generator, not by sdet-plan-generator. Records what the dedup pass examined and concluded, so a reviewer can audit a flag without re-deriving it.

condition_key.description: How 'same input condition' was computed for this run — records the operationalization so two runs can be compared.

outcome_key.description: How 'same expected outcome' was compared (e.g. exact-set).

near.description: true when the group was surfaced as near-duplicate rather than flagged

teams_in_scope.description: Every team resolved from prd_context.team[], prd_context.pdg[] and rfc_context.team_ownership[], with what each routes to. Records the teams the human excluded as well as those included, so the scope decision is auditable. The primary team also appears here.

raw_name.description: The team name as written in the PRD or RFC that matched this entry

matched_via.description: Which candidate path matched, e.g. prd.team[0], rfc.team_ownership[2]

is_primary.description: true for the team that owns the plan and its review gate

included.description: Whether the human included this team in the generated scope

browserstack_sync.description: Record of the last BrowserStack MCP upload. null until the first sync. Written by the sync, not the generator.

project.description: BrowserStack project the scenarios were uploaded to — should match the registry browserstack_project for the owning team

synced_count.description: Scenarios that received a browserstack_test_id in this sync

unsynced_count.description: Scenarios still carrying null — e.g. those owned by a team whose project was not the upload target

regression_selection.description: The executable signoff selection: existing suites CI runs alongside the new tests. Copied from regression_context.regression_selection. Holds the 'reuse' population in bulk so the plan does not carry one no-op row per already-covered case.

status.description: Human approval gate for this plan as a whole. The GENERATOR always writes 'draft' and must never write 'approved' — only a person sets that, after reading the plan and its analysis document. 'in_review' = a reviewer has picked it up. 'changes_requested' = feedback was written into the qa_analysis.md Feedback block and a Review-mode run is pending. 'approved' = cleared to flow downstream. ANY run that changes scenario content — pass2, retrigger, review — resets this to 'draft'. An approval attaches to the content that was read, not to the filename. A per-scenario `status` also exists on scenarios[] with the same four approval values plus 'deprecated'. INVARIANT: root may not be 'approved' while any scenario is still 'draft' or 'in_review' — an approved plan holding unreviewed scenarios is ambiguous. They sit at different levels so they never collide in JSON, but read the path carefully.

approved_by.description: Who approved. Set alongside status='approved'; null otherwise.

approved_at.description: When approval was given. Set alongside status='approved'; null otherwise. If updated_at is later than this, the plan changed after approval and the approval is stale.
